memory_candidates.content: Claude Code's non-interactive `claude -p` invocations from a fresh/scratch working directory are blocked by a workspace-trust-dialog gate ("this workspace has not been trusted") that fires BEFORE tool permissions, mode detection, or any skill/agent dispatch. This is more fundamental than any AskUserQuestion confirmation gate downstream. It cannot be cleared non-interactively except by pre-setting `projects["<path>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted: true` in `~/.claude.json` — a real, global, user-wide config file, not something to mutate for a throwaway scratch-dir test. Any future headless/live verification of a slash command in a fresh scratch directory should account for this gate up front (e.g., pre-configure trust, or accept the test will be BLOCKED at this gate and plan for a manual fallback).

Bash tool cwd from a `cd` in one Bash tool invocation does NOT persist into a later, separate Bash tool invocation — confirmed empirically (not just by prior GitHub issue reference) by chaining `cd "$TARGET" && pwd` in one call, then a bare `pwd` in a separate call, which reverted to the session's default cwd. Any cross-repo/root-relative shell mechanism (e.g. `cd "$GLOBAL_ROOT" && git commit ...`) must re-derive and chain the target root inline, as a single Bash call, every time it's used — never split across calls assuming persistence.
